question: Should ambiguous outbound rows with no reconciliation-capable adapter remain pending without spending retry budget—including rows already at the normal retry cap—or should OpenClaw retain a bounded terminal policy?
rationale: Both choices are internally consistent but expose different user and operator guarantees: indefinite pending preserves future reconciliation, while bounded dead-lettering limits durable state and makes failure terminal. Repository policy treats this fallback choice as maintainer-owned product behavior.

options.title: Define bounded recoverability
options.body: Preserve pending state for later reconciliation but add an explicit retention, health, and operator-recovery contract before merge.

options.title: Accept indefinite pending
options.body: Merge the current policy and explicitly accept that non-reconcilable rows may remain pending until adapter support or manual intervention arrives.

options.title: Keep bounded dead-lettering
options.body: Retain current-main terminal behavior and close or narrow this PR to diagnostics or reconciliation-capable adapters only.

recommendation.title: Define bounded recoverability
recommendation.body: Preserve pending state for later reconciliation but add an explicit retention, health, and operator-recovery contract before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Repository routing ownership and direct involvement in the PR discussion make this the strongest available owner for the cross-channel fallback-policy choice.
